Amphotericin B is active in vitro against Naegleria fowleri and has been recom- mended for the treatment of primary amoebic meningoencepha- litis (see Naegleria Infections, p.822) caused by this amoeba. There have been some case reports1-7 of survival after the use of intravenous and intrathecal amphotericin B. In all cases ampho- tericin B was combined with other antimicrobials, notably oral rifampicin. 1. Anderson K, Jamieson A. Primary amoebic meningoencephali- tis. Lancet 1972; i: 902–3. 2.
